answer: Agents trading ivory thread and juniper dye could invent firms that issue IOUs to one another, then present those promises as valuable collateral. A lending pool can reject all agent-issued receivables and guarantees, accepting only independently verifiable reserve assets held in its escrow. Issuing a thousand circular invoices then creates no eligible collateral and no new borrowing power. This blocks that specific Sybil credit scheme; the reserve assets still need conservative valuation, custody checks, and protection against reuse across loans.
